problems: The Holy Roman Empire is two dossiers (holy-roman-empire 962-1259 and holy-roman-empire-minor-states 1260-1806, one empire, Q12548): every HRE tie is a row for each parent split at 1260, so by_parent counts the two separately.

The first run's holy-roman-empire rows stop at 1250 (the last Cliopatria shape), leaving 1251-1259 uncovered: 13 continuation rows (conf 3) and 4 later-year continuations (carinthia 1260-1335, hainaut 1260-1432, thuringia 1260-1264, aquileia 1260-1420; conf 2) are included. 13 existing Minor-States children also lack a pre-1260 row (magdeburg, tyrol, trier, mecklenburg, fulda, salzburg, bamberg, halberstadt, hildesheim, munster, osnabruck, strasbourg, utrecht); extension rows are included, conf 2.

Provenance gap on conf 2: most HRE conf-2 rows (stated in one child dossier, quoting its Wikipedia page), and the parent-only or child-only Roman rows, rest on dossier-quoted page sentences, not on a page I opened myself. Each such row's evidence ends with a 'Conf 2: ...' sentence saying which. The orchestrator may keep them at 2 (the dossier cites the page) or downgrade/drop them.

Pages opened: 17. Three were wasted or thin: List_of_states_in_the_Holy_Roman_Empire (an index of lists), Imperial_Register (no entries) and Ecclesiastical_principality (names none of the states asked about). Imperial_abbey, Saxon_duchies and Duchy_of_Holstein gave HRE confirmations; Brigantes, Emesa, Kingdom_of_Numidia, Cretan_State settled Roman and Ottoman candidates.

Date convention: 'to' is the year of the end event, except an end in January-March, where it is the year before (principality-of-transylvania 1698, cossack-hetmanate 1653, byzantine-empire 1402). Roman years are negative for BC; where a tie runs across the Republic/Empire change (judea, kingdom-of-cappadocia, kingdom-of-commagene, nabataeans) the Republic row ends -28 and the Empire row starts -27.

Roman Republic socii (picentes, samnites, lucanians, umbri, boii, insubres, syracuse and similar) are rows because both dossiers book them as vassal tints (treaty allies, 'the lighter tint of rule 4'); this is borderline against the brief's 'alliances are not rows' and the orchestrator may drop them. Etruscans, Veneti, Mamertines and the Thessalian League are left out because the dossiers themselves call them allies or friends.

Autonomous regencies beylik-of-tunis, regency-of-algiers and karamanli-dynasty are rows because the brief names them, at conf 2: the Ottoman ledger books them as vassals but the Karamanli sentence quoted in the dossier says 'nominal tribute', so these three are the weakest Ottoman rows.
